reading.thesis: A Goblin swarm that is really a spell-count machine: bodies make the mana and set the copy count, one-target spells pointed at Zada turn each body into a card, a Treasure, a pump or a copy of itself, and one turn cashes the board into damage.

lines.name: fuel → conversion
lines.note: the hub's input is a single cheap spell that can legally target only Zada

lines.name: conversion → fuel
lines.note: the feedback loop that makes this an engine: four copies plus the original each draw, so one {R} returns five cards and five hasted bodies

lines.name: conversion → wincon
lines.note: 32 power, at least 30 reaching one opponent at 30 life past a single 2/2 blocker. One seat - the stack proves a kill, not a table kill

lines.name: ignition → wincon
lines.note: Dragon Fodder is one of the three casts before Empty the Warrens. The scenario stipulates the prior casts in the graveyard without their outputs (no Fodder tokens on its board), so the stack verifies the storm-count contribution only; the two tokens a real Fodder cast leaves are outside what it shows

lines.name: mana → wincon
lines.note: read carefully: stack 002's four mana come from four Mountains and both rituals are in the graveyard as two of the three prior casts. What they contribute to that burst (eight to each of two opponents, both left alive) is spell count

lines.name: wincon → output
lines.note: eight tokens, eight damage to each of two opponents. Verifiable now: validate-engine has counted cards on your own board since 2026-09-15, and Impact Tremors is on stack 002's board, which closes the previous model's open question

lines.name: wincon → output
lines.note: the three storm copies were put on the stack without being cast, so the following Grapeshot sees 4 and is five instances of one damage

lines.name: fodder → conversion
lines.note: at most ten {R}, one shot, and the last activation eats Prospector. The combo graph's infinite needs Krenko in the command zone; Zada is the commander, so the line terminates

lines.name: conversion → output
lines.note: the reason the copy spells are in the deck: each token Heat Shimmer makes through Zada is an entry, worth 1+1+2 to each opponent with all three payoffs out. Stack 017 verifies the copying half (four creatures to eight) on a board with no ETB payoff, so it cannot carry this arrow; the payoff half is oracle text plus stack 002's Tremors count. Null until a stack puts both on one board

lines.name: ignition → conversion
lines.note: with Zada, Marshal and two tokens out, Heat Shimmer at Zada alone made three hasty copies and the Marshal copy made one more Goblin: four creatures became eight. Only the copies have haste, and they are exiled at end step - a one-turn doubling, which is what a storm or pump turn wants

lines.name: conversion → fuel
lines.note: the compounding line: a board doubled by a copy spell makes the next cantrip at Zada draw twice as many. Each half rests on oracle text and stack 001; the sequence is unchecked

lines.name: fodder → conversion
lines.note: Molten Duplication copies Krenko with haste, but the copy is legendary and stack 017 shows the legend rule removing a legendary token copy, so it is a second activation only if the original has already tapped and is the one you let go. A trade, not a doubling; unchecked

lines.name: conversion → output
lines.note: the free outlet and the death trigger together price a swept or chump-blocked board at two damage per Goblin; stack 016 verifies Bombardment's half only

lines.name: fuel → wincon
lines.note: the rebuild: flashback on every instant and sorcery in the graveyard. Cast on the storm turn itself, each flashback cast continues the same storm count (storm counts every spell cast this turn); cast on a later turn, the count starts again from that turn's first spell. No stack has been run on it

open_questions.question: With Impact Tremors, General Kreat and Purphoros on the battlefield, does Heat Shimmer cast at Zada alone with N other creatures deal 4 damage to each opponent per token created, and do the copies of ETB creatures (Mogg War Marshal, Goblin Instigator, Siege-Gang Commander) add their own tokens as further entries?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Stack 017 verified the copying (four creatures to eight) on a board with no payoff. The conversion->output arrow through the copy spells is the reason v1.2.0 added them, and it stays null until one board holds both halves.

open_questions.question: With Goblin chosen, does Roaming Throne's 'triggers an additional time' apply to Zada's copy trigger, and if so is the result two full sets of copies (2N), each choosing targets separately?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This model moved Roaming Throne from protection to conversion on the oracle reading (Zada is a Goblin, her ability is a triggered ability). If it holds, every hub turn doubles; if not, Throne is a ward-{2} body and belongs back in protection or fodder.

open_questions.question: Stack 015 (Daring Discovery at Zada with three Goblins) failed its checker: is the failure a citation defect or a rules one - does each copy Discover 4?
open_questions.why_it_matters: If each copy discovers, a five-mana sorcery becomes N free spells and N storm-free casts, which would make it conversion, not fuel.

open_questions.question: Does the goldfish copy Impolite Entrance, Might of the Meek, Heat Shimmer, Molten Duplication, Electroduplicate, Twinflame, Infuriate, Ticked Off and the Treasure pumps through Zada? model-coverage lists Impolite Entrance and Might of the Meek as 'draw' only, without the 'target' channel Accelerate and Crimson Wisps carry, and the four copy spells as 'bodies, combat' only.
open_questions.why_it_matters: If the commander-copy channel does not read them, every goldfish figure prices v1.2.0's new conversion half at one copy, and a null on these cards is the model's blind spot, not the cards' weakness.

open_questions.question: What rate does the deck assemble an each-opponent ETB payoff (Impact Tremors, General Kreat or Purphoros) together with a token maker by turn six? No declared target measures this pair.
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the deck's best-verified path to damage at every opponent (stack 002 shows eight to each of its two opponents; three seats follows from the oracle's 'each opponent', not from the stack) and the stage the copy spells were added to feed.

findings.claim: One checker-passed ending and one checker-passed burst. Fists of Flame through the hub is the ending: stack 003 ...; Empty the Warrens is the wide burst: stack 002 ... who end at 24 and 20
findings.note: Round-2 fix holds. Stack 003 (checker pass) leaves its one opponent dead, so it is the ending. Stack 002 (pass) leaves both opponents alive at 24 and 20, so it is the burst. The opening sentence, the two labels and lines[2] ('the stack proves a kill, not a table kill') now agree. The evidence entries for 003 and 002 are unchanged and still correct. The mechanical check proposed in round 2 still stands: a stack cited next to 'burst' or 'not a kill' whose final_state has an opponent at life <= 0 or 'dead'.

findings.claim: The two redirect spells answer a single-target spell or ability, such as removal aimed at Zada, by changing its target; a sweeper has no target, so they do not answer one
findings.note: Round-2 fix holds, and the superlative 'best' is gone. Against the oracle text: Deflecting Swat reads 'You may choose new targets for target spell or ability', and Untimely Malfunction reads 'Change the target of target spell or ability with a single target'. Both answer a single-target spell, and neither touches an untargeted sweeper. 'Free while you control a commander' matches Swat's text ('If you control a commander, you may cast this spell without paying its mana cost'). One residual nit, not a fix item: 'does the same at instant speed' still suggests Swat is not an instant, though both are. The closing sentence's 'single-target' scoping now covers Malfunction's narrower clause.

findings.claim: engine-facts names her in six passing stacks; three concern the current 99 (001, 003, 017), since 013, 014 and 016 are about cut cards and 016 shows her not triggering
findings.note: Round-2 fix holds. Checked against decklist.txt: the cut cards are Frontline Heroism (013), Witch's Mark (014) and Spreading Insurrection (016), with 0 matches each. The current-99 focal cards are Crimson Wisps (001), Fists of Flame (003), and Heat Shimmer plus Mogg War Marshal (017), with 1 match each. All six stacks have checker verdict pass. The phrasing still undersells 013 slightly, since its spell is Crimson Wisps, a current card, and only Frontline Heroism is cut. But 'three concern the current 99' is now true, and nothing downstream sizes off it.

Up from 1674 in round 2: the fix spent 63 characters. It is 63 short of the cap, the closest of the eight stages, and the prose is still coherent. It is not muddled, but the next revision of this stage should cut a sentence before it adds one.

findings.claim: deck-audit's taplands axis counts two tapped lands: Spinerock Knoll always, and Den of the Bugbear whenever you control two or more other lands. Three more enter tapped only without enough Mountains (Arena of Glory, Castle Embereth, Dwarven Mine); deck-facts' 5 counts both groups together
findings.note: Round-2 fix holds against the oracle text. Spinerock Knoll: 'This land enters tapped.' Den: 'If you control two or more other lands, this land enters tapped.' Arena of Glory and Castle Embereth: 'unless you control a Mountain'. Dwarven Mine: 'unless you control three or more other Mountains'. deck-facts mana.enters_tapped is 5 = 2 + 3. The deck-audit misclassification of Den as unconditional is still the orchestrator's to fix: a corpus sweep over 'If you control ... enters tapped' clauses.

findings.claim: Sol Ring is the one rock; Plaza of Heroes ... the only land in the 99 that protects Zada
findings.note: Both superlatives checked by enumerating cards.json. Sol Ring is the only artifact whose text contains 'Add {'. Plaza of Heroes is the only land whose text mentions hexproof, indestructible, protection, ward or shroud.

findings.note: deck-facts (re-run this round): counts.lands 15, land_copies 36, mana.land_sources.R 29, source_targets.R 22. Unchanged from round 2.

The text of lines[] is unchanged from round 2, and every round-2 'supported' finding on lines[0..17] carries forward. Re-checked this round: each verified_by (001, 001, 003, 002, 002, 002, 002, 004, 004, 017) resolves to a stack with checker.verdict pass. validate-engine reports OK with 10/18 lines verified. The eight dashed lines (9, 11-17) are still labelled oracle arithmetic or unchecked, and none is phrased as a verified flow.

the attrition line: a clamped 1/1 dies to the -1 toughness and pays two cards, and Mogg War Marshal leaves a token when it dies. Skullclamp is invisible to the goldfish, so nothing has measured this

Squelcher gives every other creature ward, Zada included, and makes the copy spells uncounterable; unchecked

v1_stages.label: THE RED FLOOR, AND THE BURST THAT ISN'T LAND
v1_stages.what_it_does: Fifteen land entries and thirty-six copies (deck-facts), 29 of them red-producing lands by deck-facts' count and 32 red sources against a Karsten target of 22 by deck-audit's. deck-audit's taplands axis counts two tapped lands: Spinerock Knoll always, and Den of the Bugbear whenever you control two or more other lands. Three more enter tapped only without enough Mountains (Arena of Glory, Castle Embereth, Dwarven Mine); deck-facts' 5 counts both groups together. Sol Ring is the one rock. That part only has to hit drops. The part that decides games scales off the board, not off lands: Battle Hymn adds {R} per creature, Brightstone Ritual {R} per Goblin, and Three Tree City with Goblin named pays {2} to add one mana per Goblin, which is a net gain only past two Goblins. So once bodies exist, mana is downstream of the body count. Goblin Warchief sits here as a cost reducer: stack 004 locked Krenko at {1}{R}{R} because of it, and its haste is what let Krenko tap the turn he landed. Several lands are here for a second job, filed here because a land does one job in this model: Reliquary Tower (no maximum hand size, for a deck that draws a card per body off one {R}), War Room and Fountainport (a card each), Kher Keep and Sokenzan (bodies), Castle Embereth and Goblin Burrows (pumps), and Plaza of Heroes, whose exile mode gives a legendary creature hexproof and indestructible: the only land in the 99 that protects Zada. The Treasure-making pumps are NOT here; through Zada they turn bodies into mana and live in conversion.

v1_stages.label: A SECOND AND THIRD BODY BY TURN THREE
v1_stages.what_it_does: Every multiplier in this deck multiplies by creatures already on the battlefield. Zada with an empty board copies nothing; Brightstone Ritual adds one {R}; Impact Tremors fires once; Heat Shimmer copies one creature. So the first thing that has to happen is not the hub and not a ritual: it is bodies, cheaply, early. Dragon Fodder and Krenko's Command are two 1/1s for two mana; Mogg War Marshal and Goblin Instigator are two bodies off one card; Legion Warboss adds one more every turn, and Searslicer Goblin one more at each end step in which you attacked (Raid). The brief prices the declared group at 7 cards, 41.2% in an opener and 49.8% by turn three, assembling in 82.8% of games and 68.9% by turn six at mean turn 3.09 - the earliest of the three declared targets, against 4.922 for the Zada cantrip group and 6.9 for the storm payoff plus ritual. The declared group's seventh card is Skirk Prospector, which creates no tokens; it eats them, so it is held in conversion and the mismatch is filed as a proposed goldfish edit. The 3.09 is therefore the price of the group as declared, Prospector included, not of these six alone.

v1_stages.label: A CARD PER BODY
v1_stages.what_it_does: Storm counts CASTS, and stack 002 established the hard half of that: copies are put on the stack without being cast, so storm count 3 becomes 8 tokens but the next spell still sees 4. Every point of count is paid one card at a time, so the hand has to refill. Seven one- and two-mana spells target only a single creature and draw: Crimson Wisps, Expedite, Accelerate, Impolite Entrance, Renegade Tactics, Might of the Meek and Ancestral Anger. Cast at Zada alone, each is copied once per other creature, so each body becomes a card (stack 001: five cards off a single {R} with four Goblins out). That is the refill, and it scales with exactly the resource the deck builds. Around it: Goblin Matron tutors a Goblin, Conspicuous Snoop casts Goblins off the top, Grenzo impulses off combat damage, Idol of Oblivion draws once a turn after a token, and Past in Flames is the rebuild, flashback on every instant and sorcery in the graveyard after a storm turn put the hand there. Daring Discovery can legally target only Zada (up to three targets), which would make it a Discover 4 per body; stack 015 on exactly that failed its checker, so it is a candidate, not a line. deck-audit reads card-advantage at 4 counted copies against a floor of 10 and lists the cantrips as possible_uncounted: the taxonomy has no pattern for a cantrip that becomes N cards.

v1_stages.label: THE BODY PILE
v1_stages.what_it_does: Goblins are the resource this deck converts, and they are spent four ways: counted (Zada's copy count, Brightstone Ritual, Battle Hymn, Three Tree City), copied (Heat Shimmer and its kin double whatever is here), sacrificed for mana, cards or damage, and pumped for lethal. So the pile is a stage in its own right rather than a threat count. Krenko, Mob Boss is the largest repeatable producer: stack 004 measured one activation at five tokens off a four-Goblin board, because Krenko counts himself, leaving ten Goblins. Goblin Chieftain gives the pile +1/+1 and haste, which matters because most of these bodies are made the turn they are spent; Rundvelt Hordemaster pumps it and turns Goblin deaths into chances at more Goblins. Goblin Lackey puts a Goblin from hand onto the battlefield off combat damage; Impulsive Pilferer leaves a Treasure when it dies; Fable of the Mirror-Breaker makes a Goblin Shaman, loots, and flips into Reflection of Kiki-Jiki, which copies a nonlegendary creature every turn. The ignition token makers feed this pile too; they are filed apart because they are what has to happen first. Nothing here ends a game on its own, which is the correct reading of it.
cards: Fable of the Mirror-Breaker // Reflection of Kiki-Jiki

v1_stages.label: THE HUB AND WHAT IT COPIES
v1_stages.what_it_does: Zada is the multiplier: an instant or sorcery that targets only her is copied once per other creature it could target, so board size is the exchange rate (stack 001). Which spell is pointed at her decides the output, which is why single-target creature spells are engine, not filler. Ancestors' Aid, Sudden Breakthrough and Reckless Ransacking each make a Treasure: through Zada, a Treasure per body, mid-turn mana that pays for the next spell. Heat Shimmer, Molten Duplication, Electroduplicate and Twinflame each make a hasty token copy of one creature: through Zada, a copy of every creature at once, so the board doubles, every copy is an ETB for the output stage, and the next cantrip draws twice as many. Stack 017 verifies it: Heat Shimmer at Zada with Mogg War Marshal and two tokens out made three hasty copies, the Marshal copy made a fourth Goblin, and the Zada token died to the legend rule - four creatures became eight. Storm-Kiln Artist mints a Treasure per cast AND per copy (stack 005), so with Zada every copy pays. Roaming Throne naming Goblin may make Zada's trigger fire twice - an open question, and the reason it is here rather than in protection. Skirk Prospector eats a Goblin for {R} (stack 004: at most ten, one shot). Skullclamp turns a 1/1 into two cards. Goblin Bombardment converts any creature, even a stolen one (stack 016), into a point at instant speed. Zada is the single point of failure: storm copies only its own spell, so no other card copies a spell pointed at one creature. engine-facts names her in six passing stacks; three concern the current 99 (001, 003, 017), since 013, 014 and 016 are about cut cards and 016 shows her not triggering. As commander, an answer to her is a tax, not a loss.

v1_stages.label: WHERE THE BODIES LAND
v1_stages.what_it_does: Impact Tremors, General Kreat, the Boltbringer and Purphoros, God of the Forge turn a creature entering into damage to EACH opponent - one, one and two points respectively - and the deck's best-verified multi-seat damage runs through the first: stack 002 resolves eight tokens into eight damage to each of two opponents, 32 to 24 and 28 to 20. That is a burst, not a kill: both opponents end alive. This is the stage the copy spells were added to feed: every token Heat Shimmer or Empty the Warrens makes is an entry. That is a three-card class, and no declared goldfish target measures it. Pashalik Mons prices Goblin deaths instead, one point per death at any target, which is the reach that survives a sweeper. Goblin Sharpshooter prices the same deaths as pings: it untaps whenever a creature dies, so each Goblin spent to Skirk Prospector, Goblin Bombardment or Skullclamp is one more point at any target. No stack covers it yet. Siege-Gang Commander and Broadside Bombardiers buy damage with a body at a cost, and both can point it at a player. Grapeshot is filed here rather than in wincon deliberately: stack 002 measured it at storm count 4, five instances of one damage - reach and removal, not a kill across three seats at forty life.

v1_stages.label: FOUR WAYS TO KEEP ZADA
v1_stages.what_it_does: deck-audit's protection axis reads 6 copies against a 5-7 target, verdict at. Reading the six cards makes it four for the hub: Purphoros is indestructible and Roaming Throne has ward {2}, and both protect only themselves, so this model files them where they do work. The four that cover a third permanent: Swiftfoot Boots (hexproof and haste, equip {1}); Hexing Squelcher (other creatures have ward - pay 2 life, and your spells can't be countered, which protects the storm turn as well as the hub); Deflecting Swat (free while you control a commander; new targets for a spell or ability); and Untimely Malfunction, whose redirect mode does the same at instant speed and whose other modes are an artifact kill or two creatures that can't block. Plaza of Heroes is a fifth effect (hexproof and indestructible until end of turn) filed in mana. The deck's other answer to removal is structural: the rituals, Empty the Warrens, Grapeshot and Impact Tremors function with Zada in the command zone. The two redirect spells answer a single-target spell or ability, such as removal aimed at Zada, by changing its target; a sweeper has no target, so they do not answer one. That is why the pilot's interaction axis and this stage overlap.

v1_stages.label: THE ONE TURN, TWO WAYS
v1_stages.what_it_does: One checker-passed ending and one checker-passed burst. Fists of Flame through the hub is the ending: stack 003 resolves copies one at a time, each drawing first, so the +1/+0-per-card locks in at +3/+4/+5/+6 on the tokens and +7 on Zada - 32 power with trample, at least 30 of it reaching an opponent at 30 life past a lone 2/2. Empty the Warrens is the wide burst: stack 002 turns storm count 3 into eight tokens and, with Impact Tremors out, eight damage to each of two opponents - who end at 24 and 20, so it sets up a kill rather than being one. The rest are team-wide pumps only because of Zada: Wild Ride (+3/+0 and haste per body), Infuriate (+3/+2) and Ticked Off (double strike) are single-target creature spells, so through the hub each one hits the whole board. Goblin Bushwhacker kicked and Great Train Heist (untap and an extra combat, or +1/+0 and first strike) are the two that work without her. The deck's former verified loop, stack 005's Haze of Rage with Storm-Kiln Artist, is gone with Haze of Rage: v1.2.0 has no verified arbitrarily-large line, and its two contained Spellbook lines both assume Krenko is the commander, which stack 004 refutes here. deck-audit reads threat-density at 1 copy against a floor of 3 because only Ticked Off carries a wincon role; this stage is the evidence that the taxonomy cannot see a pump that becomes a team pump.

v1_map_disagreements.component: Zada online with a cantrip drawn (declared)
v1_map_disagreements.why: the group's defining property is a LEGALITY - one creature target, cheap enough to cast at Zada - and no card says that in its text. The map reads each card's other half: Accelerate, Expedite, Crimson Wisps, Renegade Tactics and Fists of Flame land in Finishers on their haste/evasion/pump text, Ancestors' Aid on its Treasure and Ancestral Anger and Wild Ride with the cheap sorceries in Ramp

Dragon Fodder and Krenko's Command are sorceries and cluster with the cheap spells, the creature token makers with the Goblins. Skirk Prospector sits in Bodies, which is right for a Goblin and still wrong for a token-maker group: it creates none, it eats them

v1_map_disagreements.component: conversion - the hub and what it copies (this model's stage)
v1_map_disagreements.why: an exchange engine is defined by what it eats and what it pays, and card text names only the payment. The sharpest case is new in v1.2.0: Heat Shimmer, Molten Duplication and Twinflame cluster in Interaction with Abrade and the redirect spells, and Electroduplicate in Ramp, though through Zada all four are the same board doubler. 'Create a token copy of target creature' reads as a one-card effect; the engine makes it N cards, and that multiplication is invisible to a model of what each card says

v1_map_disagreements.component: wincon - the one turn (this model's stage)
v1_map_disagreements.why: the team pumps are single-target creature spells that become team-wide only through Zada, so the map files Wild Ride beside the rituals and Infuriate beside the cantrips, and the taxonomy gives only Ticked Off a wincon role (deck-audit threat-density 1 against 3)

v1_map_disagreements.component: protection (this model's stage) vs the protection axis
v1_map_disagreements.why: Boots and Squelcher cluster with the equipment and utility creatures, the two redirects with the removal. The audit counts six protection copies; two of them (Purphoros, Roaming Throne) protect only themselves, which a role tag cannot distinguish from protecting the hub
